data.title: Kernel receipt names the certificate's own wire epoch; evaluator depth exhaustion is typed Unsupported

data.body: Kernel review (nit, no action required): the else arm is unreachable in practice. CheckedClaim.wire_epoch is private and set only by CheckedClaim::new (LEGACY_WIRE_EPOCH=1) and CheckedClaim::model_bound (WIRE_EPOCH=2) in verdict.rs:246-285, and wire::decode refuses every other epoch as Feature::WireEpoch (wire.rs:1183). Epoch 1 always takes the first branch, so the fallback cannot label an epoch-1 claim as model-bound. The residual risk is only a future epoch 3 being silently labeled CONTCERT/2. Consider a match on the two named constants with the fallback returning a distinct spelling, or carrying an enum instead of u16. Not blocking.

Kernel review (info, sound): Fault::DepthExhausted is produced only at model.rs:341 and model.rs:382 (depth.checked_sub(1) on the evaluator budget). Every arithmetic, lookup and domain fault still yields Overflow/OutsideDomain and stays Rejected here and in the invariant arm at :281-289. Decoder depth_bound (root=1, admits <=32) and the evaluator start budget (32, leaf needs 1) match exactly, so no decoded certificate reaches DepthExhausted. The change cannot make a false claim verify: both new outcomes are Unsupported, never Verified. With no short-circuit, an Overflow in the left operand still wins over DepthExhausted in the right.

data.reason: Kernel review (GOV 4, second non-author reviewer). Sound. DepthExhausted comes only from the evaluator budget (model.rs:341,382). Overflow and OutsideDomain stay Rejected. Decoder and evaluator depth bounds match, so it is unreachable from decoded input. No path turns a false claim into Verified. Receipt wire_epoch_id follows the private CheckedClaim.wire_epoch, which only two constructors set (1 or 2). An epoch-1 claim cannot be labeled 2, and to_json does not read the field. KCOV 01-09 pass, crate boundaries clean, tcb-audit clean. Ran kernel-core tests (113 pass), c018_checker_mutation (10) and c018_kernel_evaluator_differential (2). One nit: the receipt.rs:465 fallback. check_obligations fails only because the kernel and security reviewer entries are still missing from bn-ympz5.toml.

data.body: [risk:high assessment] Failure modes: an epoch-1 receipt could be mislabeled as epoch 2, evaluator depth exhaustion could become a certificate rejection, or arithmetic and domain defects could be diluted to Unsupported. Edge cases: legacy finite-closure and state-type claims, epoch-2 successor and invariant evaluation at depth 32, and future wire epochs. Rollback: revert 3150c657ec0f746a5c643a9a6b91d929a217fcc8 to contain a regression, while recognizing that this restores the two prior misclassifications. Monitoring: alert on Unsupported(ResourceBound(ExpressionDepth)) from any decoded certificate, and compare Receipt::wire_epoch_id with CheckedClaim::wire_epoch when minting receipts. Validation: receipt.rs:419 and :465-471 derive the accessor from the private claim epoch; verdict.rs:246-285 fixes its constructors to epochs 1 and 2; model.rs:341 and :382 are the only depth-exhaustion sources; check.rs:235-240 and :274-289 route them to Unsupported while all genuine faults remain Rejected. No path reaches Verified after either fault, and no security blocker remains.

data.reason: Security review of the full persisted range 6a16ad22a5a70e382c7fad11f3a9c389a8cf98ca..3150c657ec0f746a5c643a9a6b91d929a217fcc8: LGTM. Receipt epoch identity follows the only two private CheckedClaim constructors. Evaluator depth exhaustion cannot reach Verified, while arithmetic, domain, and closure faults remain Rejected. The risk:critical human approval gate remains separate and required.
